tasks.short: Prepare sales slips and contracts from agreed purchases.

steps.what: Confirm purchased items, customer details and agreed terms.
Enter or scan purchase details into the point-of-sale system.
Generate a sales slip or populate a contract template.
Check amounts and terms; approve contract release or escalate exceptions.
Present contracts for customer acceptance and collect required signatures.
Give the customer a copy and file the sales document.

tasks.design: Configure the point-of-sale system in {OTHER} to reuse purchase details, then generate approved templates from {DOCS} with deterministic code. Route contract exceptions through {WORKFLOW}, collect required acceptance through {ESIGN}, and file and deliver copies through {DOCS} and {EMAIL}; routine slips use existing issuance rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Purchase data and contract templates often sit apart. Bespoke terms and signatures have kept manual copying in the process.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template, signature and integration capabilities cover most of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining mapping and validation.
tasks.still_hard: Template versioning, delivery commitments and nonstandard terms need clear ownership. GDPR applies to customer data; consumer-contract requirements and employee consultation depend partly on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Explain obligations clearly, spot misunderstood terms and negotiate exceptions within delegated authority.

ambition.what: Remote customers who need signed sales contracts

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into copying details and filing documents; more goes into explaining unusual terms. Pricing and legal approval rights do not change.

reach.learn: Required order fields, delivery dependencies and amendment controls.

evidence.claim: Structured sales data can populate approved document templates without a model loop.
Electronic signature and filing workflows can reduce contract administration while preserving customer acceptance.

assumptions: This is a mixed retail setting with routine slips and some higher-value contracts.
Routine slips skip the signature step; the time split represents the combined task.
The point-of-sale system is represented by {OTHER}.
Existing automatic receipt generation offers little additional saving; gains mainly concern contracts and duplicate entry.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: The proportion of slips versus contracts and existing template automation.
Available interfaces, signature capabilities and document retention rules.
Applicable national consultation requirements and internal access lead times.
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove duplicate entry before custom code is built?
Which contract fields cause corrections after customer acceptance?
new_work: Maintain approved templates, field mappings and validation rules.
Review nonstandard terms and failed document deliveries.
Monitor signature completion and reconcile missing filed copies.

tasks.short: Inspect trade-ins, estimate their value and quote an allowance.

steps.what: Record the trade-in identity, specifications and customer-provided history.
Inspect condition, completeness and likely repair needs.
Look up comparable values in valuation databases and recent sales records.
Calculate a provisional allowance after repair costs and margin requirements.
Choose an allowance within authority or obtain approval for an exception.
Explain the allowance, conditions and expiry to the customer.

tasks.design: Use a structured trade-in record in {CRM}, with deterministic retrieval from valuation databases in {OTHER} and resale history in {ERP}. Calculate a provisional allowance using explicit repair and margin rules, then record human approval before producing the customer quote.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition is physical, comparable items differ, and valuation sources can be costly or disconnected. Calculation alone cannot settle commercial judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured inspection forms and existing data interfaces can support a small calculator and evidence view. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort without improving the underlying valuation data.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden defects, thin resale markets and uncertain repair costs remain difficult. Licensed data access and category-specific rules may dominate cost.
tasks.human_edge: Assess physical condition, recognise unreliable comparisons and explain a commercially defensible allowance.

ambition.what: Weekly review of trade-in estimates against realised resale margins

tasks.altitude: The salesperson spends less time searching and calculating, with clearer evidence for each negotiation. Allowance limits and exception approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review trade-in pricing against realised margins.
reach.learn: Repair-cost attribution, stock ageing and the difference between asking prices and realised prices.

evidence.claim: Structured valuation inputs support deterministic allowance calculations and comparison views.
Physical condition and resale uncertainty limit automated trade-in decisions.

assumptions: Trade-ins occur in durable-goods retail; this task is absent from many apparel and grocery settings.
A salesperson performs initial inspection and escalates specialist checks when required.
A spreadsheet bridges valuation evidence and commercial policy where no integrated calculator exists.
The target uses structured data and explicit rules; no model loop is necessary.
GDPR applies to customer-linked history; consultation obligations depend on national rules.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
unknowns: Trade-in categories, valuation licences and permitted data reuse.
Whether repair estimates and realised resale margins are recorded reliably.
Current pricing bands, specialist inspection requirements and approval limits.
Whether linking resale results to trade-ins is technically possible.
Access and consultation requirements for the proposed data use.
research_questions: Which valuation sources explain realised resale prices best?
Can an existing valuation screen replace the spreadsheet calculation?
How often do hidden defects outweigh the initial condition assessment?
new_work: Maintain repair rates, margin rules and comparable-item filters.
Resolve missing or stale valuation data.
Compare quoted allowances with realised outcomes and investigate large differences.

tasks.short: Bag purchases, protect merchandise and wrap gifts.

steps.what: Ask whether the customer needs bags, protective packaging or gift wrapping.
Select materials, protect items and bag or wrap the purchase.
Hand over the packed purchase and explain any handling precautions.

tasks.design: Keep packing and gift wrapping manual at a well-stocked counter. Where needed, keep short packing instructions in {DOCS}; no new application or model loop is justified.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires handling varied physical objects and materials at the counter.
tasks.enabler_now: There is no material software breakthrough for this task. Better material placement and standard packing methods are the practical improvements.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile shapes, mixed purchases and gift presentation require dexterity. Specialised machinery only makes sense for sufficiently repetitive volumes.
tasks.human_edge: Handle merchandise carefully, adapt wrapping to unusual shapes and respond to customer preferences.
tasks.altitude: The person's week and decision rights do not materially change. This remains physical customer service.

reach.task: Organise packing stations and replenish materials.
reach.learn: Material consumption, safe workstation layout and replenishment thresholds.

evidence.claim: Varied counter packing and gift wrapping remain physical tasks with little benefit from software automation.

assumptions: The task concerns varied purchases at a retail counter, not repetitive warehouse packing.
Existing packing materials and instructions remain available.
No customer tracking or employee monitoring is introduced.
Run cost describes incremental technology cost, excluding existing labour and packing materials.
Time shares are planning estimates.
unknowns: The mix of fragile items, ordinary bagging and decorative wrapping.
Packing-station layout, material shortages and peak-time queues.
research_questions: Would moving materials within easy reach remove avoidable walking?
Which items can safely leave in their existing packaging when the customer agrees?

tasks.short: Help customers try merchandise and assess its fit.

steps.what: Discuss intended use, size preferences and assistance needs.
Check available sizes and stock locations in the inventory system.
Fetch suitable sizes and prepare the fitting space.
Help the customer try items, assess fit and make suitable adjustments.
Discuss comfort and suitability, then agree on another trial or purchase.

tasks.design: Configure a quick size-and-location lookup in {OPS_SYSTEM}, using existing product and stock records. Keep the fitting conversation, physical assistance and suitability judgement with the salesperson and customer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fit depends on physical comfort, movement and customer preference. Stock lookup may already be digital but awkward to use away from a fixed terminal.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing handheld views and product-variant filters can shorten stock lookup. No model capability is required.
tasks.still_hard: Inventory can be wrong, and nominal sizes vary across merchandise. Physical assistance and the customer's comfort remain central.
tasks.human_edge: Notice discomfort, offer respectful assistance and judge fit in conversation with the customer.
tasks.altitude: The week changes little beyond shorter stock checks. The salesperson gains no new decision rights; the customer still decides what feels suitable.

reach.task: Show how product features affect use and comfort.
reach.learn: Clear demonstrations, accessibility needs and the limits of product claims.

evidence.claim: Existing inventory configuration can simplify size and location lookup without a model.
Physical fitting and customer comfort assessment remain primarily human work.

assumptions: The setting sells merchandise requiring physical fitting, such as apparel or footwear.
Stock lookup occupies a small share; most time is physical assistance and conversation.
The existing {OPS_SYSTEM} has usable size variants and stock locations.
Fitting needs remain conversational; the design does not create stored body profiles.
GDPR applies if personal fitting information is recorded; employee consultation depends on national rules.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
unknowns: Accuracy of size-level inventory and location records.
Availability of handheld access and existing lookup configuration.
Any current storage of measurements or fitting notes.
research_questions: How much fitting time is lost to stock lookup versus physically fetching items?
Can existing configuration show nearby alternatives without adding a new interface?
new_work: Report and correct stock discrepancies found during fittings.

role.altitude: Sales paperwork and valuation preparation shrink; physical service and commercial judgement remain central. Approval limits stay unchanged, while better records support informed discussions about trade-in margins.
reach: Order clerk: check sales records for fulfilment completeness.
Sales manager: compare trade-in allowances with realised margins.
Retail supervisor: improve packing-station layout and material replenishment.
Demonstrator and product promoter: explain fit-related features through clear demonstrations.
skills_to_grow: Recognise contract exceptions and explain terms clearly.
Interpret valuation evidence and resale margins.
Maintain accurate product, size and condition records.
Provide respectful fitting assistance and accessible demonstrations.
role.ambitious_version: A salesperson who supports remote contract completion and brings evidence to trade-in pricing discussions, while retaining skilled, personal service at the counter.
